To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
non-commutativity of the coordinates of a non-associative geometry can be quantized and leads to a non-singular measure.
the effective action in the non-commutativity sector can be defined in terms of a symplectic measure, and that this measure is non-singular even in the case of a degenerate Poisson structure.
non-commutativity and non-associativity are not only compatible but can be combined into a consistent theory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a non-topological deformation of string theory which may have a bearing on the problem of non-commutative geometry.
the interplay between non-commutativity and non-topological stringy effects.
the quantization of non-topological non-commuting coordinates, which are the building blocks of string theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the non-topological non-commutation of coordinates in string theory is a natural phenomenon, not only in the topological sector, but also in the general curved background.
the string world sheet, as the fundamental object in string theory, is non-commutative, but not necessarily non-associative.
non-commutativity, which in its topological sector is at the roots of both deformation quantization and string theory, also makes sense beyond the associative limit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the non-abelian generalization of the Born–Infied action is a natural framework for non-topological non-commutation in string theory.

we have found a new class of non-topological non-commmutative theories in string theory, which may be of interest for non-commutative field theory, quantum gravity, and the quantization problem of Poisson geometry.

non-commutativity can be defined in the presence of a non-vanishing B-field, but only in the presence of the RR–sector, the B-field is a genuine deformation of the symplectic geometry, which is the topological limit of non-commutative geometry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
non-associative geometry is not a pathology but a generic feature of string theory.
non-commutativity and non-associativity are ubiquitous features of string theory and can be used for the construction of new non-associative geometries.
the non-commutativity of the Poisson bracket is not a sufficient criterion to ensure non-topological non-commutation in string theory.
